highlights: The House of Representatives approved the amended draft constitution by a 421-to-8 vote on 24 August, transmitting it to the House of Peers.
House Speaker Senso Higai resigned following bipartisan criticism of his political intervention in the constitutional drafting process.
Former puppet Emperor Henry Pu Yi testified before the International Military Tribunal regarding the Kwantung Army's complete control over Manchukuo.
The Japanese Government submitted a second land reform bill to the Diet, limiting tenant holdings and enabling tenant farmer land purchases.
SCAP directives designated 505 industrial plants across eight categories, including 273 munitions facilities, for reparations custody.
Arrivals of imported American raw cotton stimulated a threefold increase in cotton yarn production over June levels.
The National Federation of Labor Unions and the National Congress of Industrial Unions held their inaugural national conventions in Tokyo.
A special first-anniversary appendix reviewed the occupation's achievements, demobilization, and economic recovery since MacArthur's landing at Atsugi on 30 August 1945.

summary: This eleventh monthly report covers August 1946 non-military activities of the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP) across occupied Japan, marking the close of the first full year of occupation. The month witnessed major constitutional and political milestones, notably the House of Representatives passing the amended draft constitution by 421 to 8 after intensive subcommittee debates, and the resignation of Speaker Senso Higai over political impartiality concerns. In the economic realm, acute food shortages prompted massive emergency distributions of imported American foodstuffs across 23 prefectures, while the Cabinet established the Price Board and submitted a second comprehensive land reform bill. U.S. cotton imports revitalized the textile industry, and SCAP placed 505 industrial facilities into reparations custody. At the International Military Tribunal for the Far East, prosecution presented evidence on aggression in China, featuring key testimony from Henry Pu Yi regarding Kwantung Army domination of Manchukuo. Historians will find especially valuable the special 33-page first-anniversary appendix reviewing occupation policies, administrative mechanisms, and statistical progress from August 1945 through August 1946.
